title: Nvidia Beat Eases AI Fears, but TCS and Infosys Face a Cautious Open
excerpt: Nvidia's $115.84 billion revenue and $130 billion forecast topped expectations, yet the relief faded in Asia and Infosys's US-listed shares fell after hours — leaving Indian IT stocks in focus, not in rally mode, on Thursday.
body:
• Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.84 billion, above the roughly $109.10 billion markets expected, with adjusted earnings per share of $2.68 against expectations of $2.48.
  • Its fourth-quarter revenue forecast of about $130 billion also beat the $125.10 billion analysts expected — the clearest sign yet that AI spending by its customers has not slowed.
  • The relief faded fast: Nvidia shares slipped 0.5% in after-hours trade after rising as much as 3.8%, and Asia-Pacific stocks erased early gains as questions over Nvidia's leadership and a reported SEC probe weighed on sentiment, Reuters reported.
  • For Indian IT holders: Infosys's US-listed shares fell 1.95% on Tuesday and a further 0.50% after hours to $12.01, and Gift Nifty slipped toward 25,255 from 25,362.50 — signals of a cautious, possibly lower, Indian open on Thursday despite the beat.

Nvidia's earnings did the job the AI trade needed: the chipmaker beat expectations on revenue and earnings and forecast more growth than analysts had pencilled in. What they did not do, at least in the first hours of Asian trade, is settle the argument about whether the AI boom has run ahead of itself — and that is why TCS, Infosys and their peers go into Thursday's Indian session in focus rather than in rally mode.

What Nvidia reported

For the quarter ended October 25, 2026, Nvidia reported revenue of $115.84 billion, up 103% from a year earlier and ahead of market expectations of approximately $109.10 billion. Adjusted earnings per share were $2.68, against expectations of $2.48. Net profit reached $65.3 billion, according to AFP. The company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of approximately $130 billion, above the $125.10 billion analysts expected.

These were the first results since co-founder Jensen Huang's abrupt departure as chief executive this month. Chairman Harvey Jones has said the board has no plans to reinstate Huang, and the company is searching for a permanent successor.

Why the relief rally faded

Asian markets opened higher — South Korea's KOSPI rose as much as 3.3% as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix gained — but the gains ebbed. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan reversed an initial rally to trade down 0.1%, and Japan's Nikkei 225 slipped 0.3%, Reuters reported. The Wall Street Journal has reported that the SEC is probing Nvidia, citing people familiar with the matter; the SEC declined to comment.

"Nvidia's results were reassuring and gave investors a reason to refocus on earnings, but they haven't resolved the broader questions around AI spending returns, financing sustainability and leadership uncertainty."

— Charu Chanana, Chief Investment Strategist, Saxo Bank, to Reuters

Wall Street had set a nervous stage: on Tuesday the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 848.75 points, or 1.64%, and the S&P 500 lost 1.03% in a fourth straight decline before the results — the sell-off we tracked in our pre-earnings coverage.

What it means for TCS, Infosys and Indian IT

The fundamental read-through for Indian IT services is reassuring: the world's largest AI spender's customers are still spending, which underwrites the cloud and AI-transformation work that fills TCS's and Infosys's order books. The price signals into Thursday are not. Infosys's American depositary receipts fell 1.95% in Tuesday's regular session and slipped another 0.50% to $12.01 after hours; Wipro lost 2.84% on the day before recovering 0.49% in extended trade to $2.06. Gift Nifty, which closed Tuesday night at 25,362.50, slipped toward 25,255 on Wednesday morning, pointing to a lower opening for Indian benchmarks even as Bank Nifty comes off a record close of 62,273.25 and the Sensex sits at 82,532.19.

In short: the earnings removed the worst-case fear — that AI demand itself was cracking — but they left the valuation and leadership questions that drove the sell-off exactly where they were.

What to watch next

Thursday's Indian open will show whether domestic investors take the demand signal or the after-hours price signal. The next test of AI appetite comes within hours: Anthropic prices its initial public offering later on Wednesday, US time, in a debut that could value the company at as much as $1.4 trillion. "I've looked at this whole week as a referendum on AI," Jake Behan, head of capital markets at Direxion, told Reuters. "Nvidia gave us a read on the buildout, and Anthropic is about to give us a read on investor appetite for the next generation of AI companies."
